properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued October 24 at 1:01AM EDT until October 24 at 1:30AM EDT by NWS Key West FL
properties.description:
SMWKEY

The National Weather Service in Key West has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Straits of Florida from Halfmoon Shoal to 20 nm west of Dry
Tortugas out 60 nm...

* Until 130 AM EDT.

* At 100 AM EDT, a strong thunderstorm was located 22 nm southwest of
Twenty-Eight Foot Shoal Light, moving south at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...National Weather Service Meteorologist.

IMPACT...Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly higher
waves, frequent lightning, and heavy downpours.

* The strong thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:
Prepare for wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, steep and fast-building
seas, frequent lightning, and blinding downpours. Stay low or go
below, and make sure all on board are wearing life jackets.

properties.areaDesc: South Central Mountains
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued October 23 at 10:45PM MDT until October 25 at 6:00AM MDT by NWS Albuquerque NM
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of central New Mexico, including the following
area, South Central Mountains.

* WHEN...Through late Saturday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be
flooded. Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Periods of light to moderate rainfall will continue overnight.
Then, shower and thunderstorm activity will redevelop Saturday
afternoon and persist through Saturday evening. Recent wildfire
burn scars in Lincoln County remain vulnerable to abrupt runoff
and flash flooding. While individual showers and thunderstorms
will typically produce rainfall amounts of 0.25 to 0.75 inch,
multiple rounds of storms will increase the risk of flash
flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/abq/EmergencyPrepFlood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

* WHEN...From 6 AM MDT Saturday through late Saturday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Creeks and streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur
in poor drainage and urban areas. Low-water crossings may be
flooded.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Showers and thunderstorms will redevelop early Saturday and
expand in coverage though the afternoon. Rainfall rates in excess

- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

dangers of flooding.
